profile.name: robo_advisor
profile.description: Conversational robo-advisor answering planning, tax, risk and product questions within the firm's methodology and policy, using the client's real portfolio through deterministic APIs and three knowledge bases; compliance-reviewed before answering.

headline: Recommended: **Router / classifier dispatch** (score +1.1; est. p50 latency ~27s vs budget 15s, ~2x tokens of one call). It exceeds the latency budget and no viable topology fits it: relax the budget, cut tool calls/reading per request, use a smaller model, or move work off the request path. The repository currently implements **Evaluator-optimizer loop** (score -5.7, ~82s); the recommendation changes the topology.

assumptions: Small-model router (~20 output tokens) then one specialist handler.

signals.rationale: 4 distinct domains: route each request to a specialist prompt/agent instead of one prompt carrying every domain's instructions and tools.
Routing to specialists gives each a small, non-overlapping tool set.

assumptions: 2 code-defined branches run concurrently, then one aggregation call.

signals.rationale: Some of the fan-out can still be code-defined if a stable first split exists.

assumptions: 4 Sonnet-tier workers in 1 wave(s) of <= 10, each with ~3 tool calls; Opus-tier lead plans and synthesises.

signals.rationale: Complex and unpredictable: a lead agent that plans and delegates handles sub-tasks that cannot be enumerated ahead of time.
~2 independent sub-tasks discovered at run time: orchestrator spawns parallel subagents, each in its own context.
Several domains inside one request: a lead delegates to domain specialists with narrow prompts and tool sets.
Tight budget: extra serial hops (planning, synthesis, critique) are expensive in wall-clock time.
Workers with narrow tool sets also remove overlap, at higher cost than routing.
Single-agent baseline is 61%: above ~45% the scaling study found negative returns from adding agents (capability saturation). Improve the model/prompt/tools instead.

assumptions: 2 sequential tool round(s) for 5 tool calls (batching by dependency=independent).

signals.rationale: Unpredictable path: the model must choose steps at run time, which is the definition of an agent.
A single agent serialises independent work, so latency grows with the number of sub-tasks.
One agent with many domains' tools and instructions becomes hard to prompt and evaluate; split when it needs more than ~10-15 well-defined tools or overlapping instructions.
Multi-hop retrieval: the model must decide follow-up queries from earlier results (agentic retrieval).

Overlapping tools are OpenAI's split trigger (systems fail with <10 overlapping tools yet manage 15+ distinct ones): first consolidate/rename tools; if that fails, give each specialist a disjoint tool set.
A 61% single-agent baseline is the regime where one agent plus a better model/effort/tools wins.

assumptions: One handoff per request assumed (specialist A -> B); each handoff re-briefs the next agent.

signals.rationale: Multi-turn conversation crossing specialist domains: decentralised handoffs let the right specialist own the user at each moment.
Single-agent baseline is 61%: above ~45% the scaling study found negative returns from adding agents (capability saturation). Improve the model/prompt/tools instead.

assumptions: 5 parallel claude-opus-5 samples; majority vote in code (no judge call).
4 sequential stages with programmatic gates between them.

signals.rationale: A fixed chain cannot handle a path that varies per request.

assumptions: 3 generate/evaluate iterations (worst case); most requests exit after the first accepted evaluation.

signals.rationale: Tight budget: extra serial hops (planning, synthesis, critique) are expensive in wall-clock time.

assumptions: 4 leads x 2 workers; two delegation levels add two extra plan/synthesis hops.

signals.rationale: Tight budget: extra serial hops (planning, synthesis, critique) are expensive in wall-clock time.
Single-agent baseline is 61%: above ~45% the scaling study found negative returns from adding agents (capability saturation). Improve the model/prompt/tools instead.

augmentations.title: Build a ~20-query eval before adding any structure
augmentations.why: Every source agrees: measure a single agent/call first, then add topology only where the eval shows it failing. Above a ~45% single-agent baseline, adding agents tended to hurt in the scaling study. Keep the eval to compare latency and accuracy across topologies.

augmentations.title: Prompt caching on the stable prefix (system prompt, tool schemas, reference docs)
augmentations.why: Multi-turn and multi-call topologies re-send the same prefix on every call; caching cuts cost up to ~90% and time-to-first-token.

augmentations.title: Structured outputs (JSON schema) for routers, extractors and votes
augmentations.why: Removes parsing failures and makes code-side gates and majority votes trivial.

augmentations.title: Parallel tool use inside each agent turn
augmentations.why: Independent tool calls issued in one assistant turn cut rounds by 2-4x; return all results in one message.

augmentations.title: Context editing (clear stale tool results/thinking)
augmentations.why: Keeps long loops lean without summarisation losses.

augmentations.title: Memory across sessions (file/DB-backed)
augmentations.why: State that must outlive one conversation should be written to memory, not carried in context.

augmentations.title: Dedicated, gated tools for irreversible actions with human approval
augmentations.why: Promote side-effecting actions to typed tools so the harness can intercept, confirm, audit and roll back; never let them run through a generic shell tool.

augmentations.title: Model tiering: large model for planning/synthesis, smaller models for reading/routing
augmentations.why: Reading-heavy workers and routers need many input tokens and little judgment; run them on Sonnet/Haiku and keep Opus for the lead.

augmentations.title: Agentic retrieval capped at ~4 iterations: start broad, then narrow
augmentations.why: Multi-hop retrieval buys accuracy (27% -> 43% EM on HotpotQA) at 3-20x latency; cap the loop and prefer short broad queries first, narrowing progressively.

report_card.name: robo_advisor
report_card.summary: Full report card for **robo_advisor**: overall **F** (54.1/100). Task complexity 5 (open-ended), design 4 (complex), behaviour 5 (open-ended). Priority: Loops without limits. Weakest dimension: Latency (F). Agents needing attention: agent.

dimensions.name: Outcome quality
findings: Only 35% of repeated tasks agree on outcome across runs: reliability across runs is low (Galileo reports 60% single-run falling to 25% over eight runs).
Measured success 48% is below the stated single-agent baseline 61%: the added structure is not paying for itself.
Success 48% is above the ~45% capability-saturation threshold: adding agents is unlikely to help; improve model, prompt or tools instead.

dimensions.name: Reliability and control
findings: 31% of runs repeat an identical tool call (step repetition is 15.7% of multi-agent failures in MAST). Add a result cache or a rule against re-calling with the same arguments.

9% of runs end by hitting a step or recursion limit: the agent does not know when it is done ('unaware of termination', 12.4% of failures). Add explicit stop criteria to the prompt and check the limit is not too low.
Tool error rate 10%: return `is_error` results the model can act on, and add retries with backoff in the harness.

dimensions.name: Latency
findings: p95 latency 44.4s is 3.0x the budget: the tail is driven by long tool chains or loops.

dimensions.name: Governance and guardrails
findings: Loops or delegation without termination limits in code.
High-stakes outputs without schema-validated structured output.
Traces show no human approval steps despite irreversible tools.

mismatches.title: Loops without limits
mismatches.detail: Repetition in 31% of runs, 9% hit a limit, and no termination limits are in code.
mismatches.action: Add max turns/tool calls/iterations and explicit stop criteria; cache identical tool calls.

mismatches.title: Overlapping tools
mismatches.detail: 3 tools share a name stem (search_methodology, search_policy, search_products).
mismatches.action: Consolidate or namespace tools; overlap, not count, is what confuses agents (OpenAI).

findings: repeats identical tool calls in 31% of runs
stable: no loops, low variance, no tool errors
